title: Polynomial behaviour
examples: How do I know the end behaviour just from the factored form?
If a root has a multiplicity of three, what does the graph do there?
Does the number of turning points always relate to the degree?

explain.say: Let us look at the end behaviour of a polynomial graph. The end behaviour is what happens when x gets very large or very small. We only need to look at the leading term to predict this behaviour.

items: End behaviour: what happens when x is very large or very small
Look at the leading term to predict behaviour

explain.say: If the leading term has an even degree, the graph goes in the same direction on both ends. For example, if the leading term is x squared, both ends go up. This means the graph goes to positive infinity on both sides.

If the leading term has an odd degree, the graph goes in opposite directions on both ends. For example, if the leading term is x cubed, the left end goes down and the right end goes up. This is a common pattern.

The multiplicity of a root tells us how the graph crosses the x axis. If the multiplicity is odd, the graph crosses straight through the axis. If the multiplicity is even, the graph just touches and turns around at the axis.

items: Degree n: at most n minus one turning points
Cubic polynomial: at most two turning points

explain.say: A polynomial of degree n can have at most n minus one turning points. For instance, a cubic polynomial can have at most two turning points. This gives a good check for your sketch.

faq.q: What does the leading term really mean for the end behaviour?
faq.a: The leading term is the term with the highest power of x. You only need to look at its coefficient and its degree to see where the graph heads.
asks: How do I find the end behaviour?
What part of the polynomial matters most for the ends?

faq.q: If a root has a multiplicity of two, what does the graph do there?
faq.a: The graph will touch the x axis at that root and immediately turn back in the direction it came from. It does not cross the axis.
asks: Does multiplicity two mean it bounces?
What happens at an even multiplicity root?

faq.q: Can a polynomial have more turning points than its degree minus one?
faq.a: No, a polynomial of degree n can have at most n minus one turning points. This is a useful limit when sketching the graph.
asks: Is n-1 the maximum number of turning points?
Can I have more turning points than the degree minus one?

faq.q: How do I use the factored form to sketch the graph?
faq.a: First, find the roots from the factors. Then, use the multiplicity rules to guide your sketch. Finally, check the end behaviour.
asks: What is the best way to sketch from factors?
What order should I follow when sketching?

faq.q: Does the sign of the leading coefficient matter for the end behaviour?
faq.a: Yes, the sign tells you if both ends go up or both ends go down. A positive coefficient means both ends go up if the degree is even.
asks: Does the sign of the first term matter?
What if the leading coefficient is negative?

facts: The end behaviour is determined by the leading term of the polynomial.
If the degree is even, the graph approaches the same y-value on both ends.
If the degree is odd, the graph approaches opposite y-values on the two ends.
An odd multiplicity root causes the graph to cross the x-axis.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n minus one turning points.

quiz.say: Consider a polynomial with a leading term of 3 x squared. What is the end behaviour?
quiz.why: Since the degree is two, which is even, and the coefficient is positive, both ends must go up.

wrong.0: This pattern belongs to polynomials with an odd degree.
wrong.1: The degree and the sign of the leading coefficient always predict the end behaviour.
wrong.3: This would only happen if the leading coefficient was negative.

quiz.say: A factor is (x - 2) squared. What does this imply about the graph at x = 2?

options.show: The graph has a vertical asymptote
options.say: The graph has a vertical asymptote

options.show: The graph is undefined at x=2
options.say: The graph is undefined at x=2

quiz.why: The multiplicity of two is even, so the graph only touches the axis and turns around.

wrong.0: This describes rational functions, not polynomial factors.
wrong.1: Since it is a factor, the function is perfectly defined at that root.
wrong.3: Crossing straight through only happens when the multiplicity is odd.

quiz.say: A polynomial has a degree of five and factors like x(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)(x-4). What is the end behaviour?
quiz.show: End behaviour: Left down, right up

options.show: The end behaviour is not predictable
options.say: The end behaviour is not predictable

quiz.why: The degree is five, which is odd. The leading coefficient is positive, so the left end goes down and the right end goes up.

wrong.0: For polynomials, the end behaviour is always predictable from the degree and leading coefficient.
wrong.2: This suggests an even degree, but the degree given is five.
wrong.3: This would require the leading coefficient to be negative.
